A consumer who speaks up is stronger than a company that avoids accountability.   Arjun had saved his hard-earned money with great hope and ordered an expensive jacket worth ₹26,000 from Myntra. When the parcel arrived, he was excited. But the moment he opened the box, his happiness turned into shock.  Instead of the ₹26,000 jacket, the package contained a pair of shorts worth barely ₹150.  Imagine what he must have felt. His money was gone, his trust was broken, and all he received was disappointment.  Arjun immediately initiated a return. Days turned into weeks, and weeks into months, but his refund never arrived. Every time he contacted customer support, he received the same response: “Sir, we are investigating the matter.” He was forced to repeatedly follow up just to recover his own money, causing immense stress and sleepless nights.  But Arjun refused to give up. Instead of accepting the situation, he approached the Consumer Court.  During the hearing, the company argued that the mistake was not theirs but the seller's.  However, the court made it clear that the customer had placed his trust in the platform and paid the platform. The company could not escape responsibility by blaming a third-party seller.  The verdict was significant. The court ordered Myntra to refund the full ₹26,000 and also pay ₹50,000 as compensation for the mental harassment caused to the customer.  This case sends an important message: online platforms cannot avoid responsibility by shifting the blame to sellers. When customers purchase through a platform, the platform is accountable for resolving such issues.  A valuable lesson for every online shopper: always record an unboxing video when receiving expensive items such as phones, laptops, or branded clothing. It can serve as crucial evidence if something goes wrong.  If you ever face a similar issue, don't stay silent. You can file a complaint through the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or submit a case online through the e-Daakhil portal.  Arjun Kumar's determination is an inspiration for millions of consumers who often feel powerless against large companies. His fight is a reminder that consumers have rights—and with persistence, justice can prevail.
